title: Bibimbap
subtitle: Korean rice bowl with vegetables, beef, and gochujang
excerpt: A bowl of warm rice topped with individually seasoned vegetables, minced beef, a fried egg, and a spoonful of gochujang chilli paste. Everything mixed together at the table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bibimbap (literally 'mixed rice') is one of the most widely eaten Korean dishes both in Korea and internationally. The dish is thought to have originated as a way of using up leftover namul (seasoned vegetable dishes) from celebratory meals, served over rice. Each component is seasoned and cooked separately, which is what gives the dish its distinct flavours and textures: cooked separately, each vegetable retains its own character. The defining condiment is gochujang (fermented red chilli paste), which is mixed in at the table. Dolsot bibimbap, served in a sizzling stone bowl that crisps the bottom layer of rice, is a celebrated restaurant version.

content.text: Each topping is cooked and seasoned separately before it goes on the rice. This takes more time than a one-pot dish but is what makes bibimbap taste right: each vegetable should be distinct, not blended together. The gochujang goes on top at the end and is mixed in at the table by each person to their own heat preference. Start by putting the rice on, then work through each topping while it cooks.
Cook the rice according to the absorption method: rinse, add to a pan with 600 ml cold water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Rest off the heat for 10 minutes.

Season the beef with 2 tablespoons of soy sauce and 1 clove of minced garlic. Fry in a hot pan with a little oil for 5 minutes until cooked through. Set aside. Wipe the pan and fry each vegetable separately: courgette 2 minutes, carrots 3 minutes, mushrooms 4 minutes, bean sprouts 2 minutes, spinach 1 minute. Season each with a little soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic as you go.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in a little oil so the yolk is still runny.

Divide the rice between four bowls. Arrange portions of each vegetable and the beef in sections around the bowl. Place the egg on top. Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve with a spoonful of gochujang on top. Mix everything together before eating.
